tonight.headline: Your kicker slot is empty. Fill it and you're the favourite
body: Jason Myers was dropped at 04:39 UTC when Rashod Bateman came in, and no kicker replaced him. ESPN is counting a zero at K, and projects you 109.6 to JuiceJam's 112.1 (49%). A free-agent kicker adds about 8.6 and makes you the favourite.
Thursday: Matthew Golden scored 21.0 and MarShawn Lloyd 3.8, both on your bench. JuiceJam have 6.6 from Tucker Kraft, and they still start Nico Collins at 0.0.

case.label: The Collins hole
case.body: The Houston Chronicle expect Collins (hamstring) to miss again. If JuiceJam swap in Jameson Williams (11.0), they go to about 123. You'd be about 118 with a kicker, so the kicker alone doesn't win it. It does stop you conceding nine points for nothing.

case.label: Golden on the bench
case.body: Tate over Golden was a projection coin flip, 11.8 to 11.4, with no thesis. Golden went 5-100-1. That's one box score, not a reason to change the method.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: JuiceJam leaving Collins in the lineup. Then a filled kicker slot puts you roughly 15 ahead on projection.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Free agent, no priority. Do it now, before someone else takes him. Little kicks off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Add Cam Little (K). Drop Colston Loveland
doFirst.subtitle: THE DROP IS LOVELAND. Not Bateman, not Vele, not Tuten. Free-agent add, so waiver priority stays at 6.

case.label: The slot
case.body: You have no kicker. Myers went out at 04:39 UTC with the Bateman add, and ESPN projects a 0.0 there. An empty mandatory slot costs more than churn. The Chem defence precedent (24 Sep) broke the seven-day rule for the same reason.

case.label: The kicker
case.body: Cam Little is a free agent at 85.9% owned. Yahoo's Week 3 board (22 Sep) has him K2, at home against New England. ESPN disagrees: it has Pineiro 9.8 to Little 8.6. I side with the outside boards because three have Pineiro outside their top 12: Yahoo leaves him off, ClutchPoints have him 15th, PFN 17th. He also didn't attempt a field goal in Week 2. Pineiro is the acceptable second choice. Myers is on waivers until Saturday, so re-adding him would cost priority.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Loveland is 94.5% owned, and dropping him disagrees with the market on the record. He has drawn 3 and 4.5 opportunities for 0.7 points a game, and the waiver tool flags him FALLING in every week. Chicago are now preparing Case Keenum, their third-string quarterback, after Caleb Williams missed Wednesday and Thursday and Tyson Bagent stayed in concussion protocol (National Football Post, PhiladelphiaEagles.com). Gadsden already has the tight-end slot. Hunter Henry (10.1) and Jake Ferguson are free agents who project above Loveland, so tight-end depth can be replaced for nothing any day.

case.label: Why not the others
case.body: Vele played 96% of the Saints' snaps in Week 2 (Yahoo). Tuten is Barkley's cover and the Lamar trade piece. Dropping Bateman would reverse a move made eight hours ago, and he's about to have a real role: SI call Flowers playing 'shocking'. Golden and Lloyd have already played, so they're locked.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Loveland draws six or more targets on Monday with Keenum, or clears 60% of routes with five-plus targets in two games once Williams is back. Then the market was right and he was worth the seat. The kicker half is wrong if Little finishes outside the top 15 while Pineiro finishes top five.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Decide on Friday's Ravens ruling, before Tate's 11:00 Sunday kickoff (Bateman plays 14:25)
doFirst.title: Only if Baltimore rule Flowers out: start Bateman over Tate in the flex
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Swap only, nothing dropped. If Flowers is listed anything but OUT, leave Tate in.

case.label: The role fact
case.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) didn't practise Wednesday or Thursday. SI (24 Sep) say it would be 'shocking' if he played in Rio, and Rapoport said the DNP doesn't bode well (Yahoo). In Week 2, without Flowers, Bateman drew 9 targets.

case.label: The volume
case.body: Week 2 opportunities: Bateman 13.5, Tate 7.5, a clear volume gap. Tate has 11 targets in two games for 6.8 a game. That's a role, but a smaller one.

case.label: Against it
case.body: ESPN projects Tate 11.8 to Bateman 7.6. The 7.6 looks like it prices a healthy Flowers, but I can't prove that. Tate's matchup is better too: the Giants have allowed the 22nd-fewest WR points, Dallas the 15th-fewest (footballdb). If ESPN moves Bateman above Tate after the ruling, this becomes an easy call.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Flowers plays. Or Bateman draws fewer than six targets while Tate outscores him, which closes the thesis WRONG.

action.label: Start Bateman · bench Tate (only if Flowers is out)

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Decide on Saturday's Eagles report, before Tuten's 11:00 Sunday kickoff
doFirst.title: Only if Philadelphia rule Barkley out or doubtful: start Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed, and less likely than yesterday. Barkley says he expects to play.

case.label: What changed
case.body: Barkley was limited on Thursday with the stinger (PhiladelphiaEagles.com) and told reporters he expects to play (NBC Sports, 24 Sep).

case.label: The timing trap
case.body: Barkley plays Monday; Tuten plays Sunday. If Barkley is still questionable going into Monday, Tuten has already locked. Standing policy: a top-12 back who is only questionable starts. Only OUT or DOUBTFUL on Saturday moves him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Barkley is listed full on Friday or carries no designation on Saturday. The card then never fires.

action.label: Start Tuten · bench Barkley (only if Barkley is out)

whatWentWrong.title: Your kicker slot has been empty since 04:39 UTC
whatWentWrong.lead: Bateman came in for Jason Myers overnight, and nothing replaced Myers. This is the second time in three days that a paired move has emptied a mandatory slot. The Chem D/ST went the same way on 23 Sep.

case.label: What happened
case.body: At 04:34 you put Gadsden in for Loveland. At 04:39 you added Bateman, and the drop was the kicker. Yesterday's brief listed Bateman as a WATCH row, with the note that there was no seat for him.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The first card fills the slot, and it states the drop on its own line: Loveland. Whenever an add needs a drop, check the drop isn't your only K or D/ST.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If the Myers drop was deliberate and a kicker add is already planned, just make sure it happens before Sunday 11:00. The snapshot shows no kicker on the roster.

roster.footnote: Golden and Lloyd played Thursday; their actuals are shown. Everyone else plays Sunday, and Barkley and Loveland play Monday at 18:15. There's no kicker row because the roster has no kicker. Grades use footballdb's 2026 table: standard scoring, two games, 1st = fewest allowed. That's a thin sample. Times are Mexico City.

lineupCheck.verdict: The tool prefers Loveland over Gadsden on volume (4 to 3) and projection (9.7 to 8.7). Overridden on a named quarterback fact: Chicago are preparing third-string Case Keenum. The tool can't see that the K slot is empty, which costs about 8.6 on its own; the first card fixes it.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.6 a week. Tuten replaces Rachaad White's 9.4 at RB2, and Lamar scores them nothing sitting behind Josh Allen.

case.label: Re-checked this morning
case.body: Recomputed from the 12:53 UTC snapshot. Lamar is still in slot 20 behind Allen in slot 0, and White still starts at RB2. Your best lineup goes 110.7 to 114.4 (both without a kicker); Team 13's goes 123.6 to 125.2. Lamar isn't on Baltimore's report (SI, 24 Sep).

case.label: Honest risk
case.body: On season projections it's lopsided: Lamar 297.3, Tuten 166.9. That's why it's a longshot; it only works for them on a weekly lineup view. It also removes Barkley's cover while Barkley has a stinger.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 start a second real back or trade a quarterback, Lamar lands on Baltimore's report, or Barkley is ruled out and Tuten has to start. Don't send it again. Only respond if they open the conversation.

trades.copyText: Hi, would you do Lamar for Bhayshul Tuten? Lamar sits behind Allen and can't score for you, and Tuten goes straight into your RB2 ahead of White. That's about +1.6 a week to your lineup. Propose it in ESPN if you're in.

worthALook.name: Adonai Mitchell
worthALook.lead: The receiver taking targets from your own starter. The finger injury looks minor.

case.label: The role
case.body: Team-high 12 targets in Week 2. The Jets have four healthy receivers and no Mason Taylor.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Went from not listed Wednesday to limited Thursday with the finger (NewYorkJets.com, RotoBaller).

case.label: When to act
case.body: If he again out-targets Garrett Wilson at Detroit. Wrong if Wilson draws nine or more targets and Mitchell fewer than six. He's a free agent, but there's no seat until the kicker is solved.

worthALook.name: Josh Downs
worthALook.lead: A real role, and still no seat.

case.label: The role
case.body: Nine targets after Alec Pierce left in Week 2 (NBC Sports). Pierce (heel) then went on IR (NBC Sports, 23 Sep), so this lasts at least four weeks. Houston have allowed the most WR points in the league (footballdb).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Your seats this week go to the kicker. Golden (21.0 Thursday), Vele and Bateman already crowd the WR bench.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Next week, if Tate stays under five targets on Sunday. He's a free agent, so it costs no priority.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN has Carolina 7.3 to the Giants' 7.1. Jaelan Phillips returned to full practice Thursday, but Devin Lloyd (calf) was held out again (Panthers.com).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: A 0.2 gap doesn't justify a roster move, and this week's move goes to the kicker.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only if the Giants lose another pass rusher on Friday's report on top of Burns.

doNotChase.name: Jason Myers
doNotChase.lead: Your own dropped kicker. Don't claim him back.

case.label: The fact
case.body: He's on waivers until Saturday 01:00 Mexico City. Yahoo have him K5 this week, so he's a fine kicker.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: A claim drops you from waiver priority 6 to 10 for the rest of the season. Cam Little is a free agent today and ranks higher (K2) on the same board.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If he clears unclaimed he becomes a free agent again, but the kicker seat is filled by then.

doNotChase.name: Tyler Shough
doNotChase.lead: He projects above Lawrence and he's free. The case for him is box scores.

case.label: The case for
case.body: 27 of 34 for 252 in the Week 2 comeback (Yahoo). ESPN projects him 17.7 to Lawrence's 16.4.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: This quarterback slot has already lost 42.8 points to chasing box scores. Lawrence has no injury, and Las Vegas have allowed the 6th-fewest QB points (footballdb), so the matchup isn't softer.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Lawrence getting hurt. Shough is then the free-agent answer, and you carry no backup quarterback.

doNotChase.name: Josh Jacobs
doNotChase.lead: The best-looking name on the wire, and he isn't playing.

case.label: The fact
case.body: Still on the Commissioner's Exempt List (NFL.com, ESPN); he missed Thursday's game. ESPN labels him DAY_TO_DAY with a 167.6 season projection, and neither reflects that.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The NFL reinstates him AND Green Bay activate him. Even then, Lloyd is already on your roster.

doNotChase.name: Tank Bigsby
doNotChase.lead: A handcuff to your own back, and Barkley expects to play.

case.label: The fact
case.body: All of his rise (1 opportunity, then 16) came while Barkley played through the stinger. Barkley was limited Thursday and says he expects to play (NBC Sports).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley is ruled out for more than a week and Bigsby is named the lead back. Tuten covers first either way.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Eight risers and two fallers, from only two weeks of data, which is thin. One becomes a move: Loveland (FALLING) is the drop for the kicker, because the data and a named quarterback fact point the same way. None of the risers is an add today; the only open seat goes to the kicker.

falling.roleReason: Low usage even with Caleb Williams. Now Williams (hamstring) and Bagent (concussion) both missed Wed and Thu, and Chicago are preparing third-string Case Keenum (National Football Post, PhiladelphiaEagles.com)

settled.result: Thursday: 3.8 PPR. Green Bay ran for 17 yards, and PFF call it a near-even split with Chris Brooks. It sat on your bench, so no cost. One week against the thesis; it closes WRONG if Brooks or Johnson out-touch him again next week.

settled.result: Flowers has not practised all week and SI call a return 'shocking'. The decline's own condition is about to fire. You added him anyway at 04:39, but the drop that came with it was the kicker.

settled.title: Claim Jonah Coleman with never-resetting priority (23 Sep)
settled.result: He didn't practise all week and was dropped without playing. Priority went 3 → 6, permanently.

settled.title: Don't claim Carnell Tate; take him if he clears (23 Sep)
settled.result: He cleared unclaimed and you added him free. Priority is still 6, and he's in your flex.

cannotSee.body: Flowers' ruling (Friday), Barkley's and Williams' designations (Saturday, for a Monday game) all come after this brief. The two fallback cards wait for them.

cannotSee.label: Whether JuiceJam fix Collins
cannotSee.body: Your odds depend on whether they leave a 0.0 in the lineup. Nothing here can see what they'll do.

cannotSee.label: The kicker boards disagree
cannotSee.body: ESPN has Pineiro above Little by 1.2 points; Yahoo, ClutchPoints and PFN rank Pineiro much lower. Kicker scoring is noisy week to week, so filling the slot matters far more than which of the two you pick.

cannotSee.label: The lineup tool's blind spot
cannotSee.body: lineup_check.py compares players it can see, so it reported a 1.0 gap and missed the empty kicker slot entirely.

cannotSee.body: Grades come from footballdb's 2026 table: standard scoring, not PPR, and only two games.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims
cannotSee.body: ESPN only returns your own pending claims, so nobody else's queued claims are visible.

cannotSee.body: The Lamar row is priced on this week's lineups. Season numbers call it lopsided, which is why it's a longshot.
